newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says Erhard policies still relevant today.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says Erhard policies still relevant today.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Wednesday the policies of Ludwig Erhard, father of Germany's post-war "economic miracle," remained valid for present-day policymakers faced with the challenge of globalisation.

But the chancellor, who used the 100th anniversary of Erhard's birth to link the legendary economist to his own economic policy, made no specific suggestions for lessons to be learned from the early years of Bonn's Federal Republic.
Kohl even dropped a planned speech at the end of a solemn commemorative ceremony in Bonn attended by about 2,000 guests from politics, business and the arts.
Officials said Kohl, who had made introductory remarks before a former associate of Erhard's gave the main speech, changed his plans because the ceremony was running late.
In his planned speech, which was distributed to journalists, Kohl said Erhard set an example of optimism, hard work and unbureaucratic policies that later generations should follow.
"Ludwig Erhard would without a doubt have stood in the vanguard of those who would argue to quickly use the opportunity globalisation offers," the text said.

"He would have tried to convince people that holding on to privileges and expecting the state to take care of them would not lead to a good future. Only an open mind, mobility and readiness to change would do that."

Erhard, who would have been 100 years old on February 4, became a legend here by introducing the deutschemark in 1948, liberalising West Germany's shattered economy and creating a "capitalism with a social conscience".
